To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the perception of object size is influenced by explicit feedback of action success.
explicit feedback of action success and failure affects the size estimation of target objects independently of the actual action success.

the explicit feedback regarding movement failure leads to a perceptual bias of the target object size in the direction of a smaller size than the actual size of the target, whereas the feedback regarding movement success leads to a perceptually larger size of the target object than its actual size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how the perception of objects and the performance of actions are related.
a new phenomenon, which is not related to actual action success but rather to the actor's explicit knowledge about success and failure of action.
the impact of the explicit evaluation of one's own motor action on visual perception.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
action feedback affects the perceived size of action-related objects, but that this effect is independent of the actual action outcome.
action feedback influences the perception of action related objects, but the effect of action feedback on object perception is not a simple reflection of the actual action success.
the perception of target objects is affected by the explicit knowledge of an actor's own movement outcome, regardless of the actual motor success.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
action success feedback is not just a consequence of the actual action success but also a consequence of an actor's evaluation of his/her action.
the explicit knowledge of an action outcome, rather than the actual action outcome, affects the perception of target objects.
the perception of objects is biased by the actor's explicit evaluation of the motor action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
action success feedback may affect perception of action targets independently from the actual action success.
the explicit feedback regarding movement outcome can influence perception of target size independently from the actual movement success.
the perception of action-relevant objects can be influenced by the explicit knowledge of an action outcome, independently of actual action ability.
